propositions: When a Jira issue moves between projects, its KEY changes but its numeric ID remains immutable; bindings keyed on the mutable KEY can silently detach if the moved_issue_key table is not updated by third-party movers.

The binding store must persist the numeric issue ID alongside the KEY and fall back to resolving by ID when a KEY lookup fails, then re-key the binding to the issue's current KEY to maintain consistency.

On a failed KEY lookup, the system retries using the recorded numeric ID; if the ID resolves to a different KEY, the binding is updated, the reverse index is maintained in the same operation, and the issue is treated as present rather than absent.
Pre-existing bindings without a recorded ID continue to work unchanged without migration, degrading gracefully to the current behavior when no fallback is available.
The ID fallback is not invoked while the KEY resolves normally, preserving the happy-path performance of the absence probe.
Cloud-facing methods that take jira_key as a parameter maintain their existing signatures and semantics, keeping the shared binding store unchanged for Cloud deployments.
